nodes.summary: For a normal operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space, a bounded $E$ and a point $\mu$ of the spectrum of $A + E$, some point of the spectrum of $A$ is within $\|E\|$ of $\mu$: the distance to the compact spectrum is attained.
nodes.title: Attained form of the Bauer–Fike theorem for normal operators

nodes.summary: Let $A = V \Lambda V^{-1}$ be a diagonalizable complex $n \times n$ matrix, $\Lambda = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n)$, and let $E$ be any complex $n \times n$ matrix. Every eigenvalue $\mu$ of $A + E$ satisfies
nodes.title: Bauer–Fike theorem for diagonalizable matrices

nodes.summary: For self-adjoint `A` and `A + E`, the Hausdorff distance of the two spectra is at most `‖E‖`.
nodes.title: Hausdorff distance between spectra of self-adjoint perturbations

nodes.summary: For a normal operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space and any bounded perturbation $E$, every point of the spectrum of $A + E$ lies within $\|E\|$ of the spectrum of $A$. For a normal matrix this is the Bauer–Fike theorem with a unitary eigenvector matrix $V$, so that $\kappa_2(V) = 1$.
nodes.title: Bauer–Fike theorem for normal operators

nodes.summary: The resolvent norm bound for a normal operator: if `z` lies outside the spectrum of a normal `A`, then `‖(z • 1 - A)⁻¹‖ ≤ 1 / dist z (spectrum ℂ A)`.
nodes.title: Resolvent norm bound for a normal operator
